subtopic: Tensor Core density vs FP32 SIMT
learningObjective: Compare the arithmetic density (FLOP per cycle per SM) of NVIDIA Tensor Core FP16 vs FP32 SIMT paths, and reason about when each dominates.
stem: A100 SXM published peaks: FP32 CUDA-core ≈ 19.5 TFLOP/s; FP16 Tensor Core ≈ 312 TFLOP/s (dense). A GEMM kernel with sufficient AI can, in principle, choose between the two paths. Which statement about the Tensor Core vs CUDA-core throughput ratio is correct?

options.text: The FP16 Tensor Core path is roughly 16× more FLOP-dense than the FP32 CUDA-core path on A100; using FP16 tensor cores (when the workload tolerates FP16 precision) yields up to a 16× ideal speedup for compute-bound kernels.
The FP16 Tensor Core path is roughly 2× denser than FP32 CUDA cores because Tensor Cores process 2 operands per lane in one instruction; the ratio 312 / 19.5 must be a benchmark artifact.
The FP16 Tensor Core path halves throughput compared to FP32 CUDA cores because reduced precision requires additional accumulation steps.
The paths are equal in throughput; the 312 TFLOP/s figure counts sparse Tensor Core throughput, which reduces to ~19.5 TFLOP/s once sparsity is disabled.

explanation: 312 / 19.5 ≈ 16. This is the documented dense-throughput ratio on A100 SXM between FP16 Tensor Cores and FP32 CUDA cores. Compute-bound kernels that can tolerate FP16 (with FP32 accumulation) can approach this speedup; memory-bound kernels benefit less because HBM bandwidth is unchanged. Options B, C, D contradict the documented peak numbers.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: 312 / 19.5 ≈ 16× dense; the actual ideal speedup applies only to compute-bound workloads that can adopt the FP16 tensor core path.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: the ratio is ~16×, not ~2×; A100 dense Tensor Core figures are architectural, not benchmark artifacts.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: FP16 Tensor Core throughput exceeds FP32 CUDA-core throughput; extra accumulation does not net a slowdown at the kernel level.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the 312 TFLOP/s figure is dense (not sparse). Sparse throughput would be ~624 TFLOP/s under 2:4 structured sparsity.

assumptions: A100 SXM dense FP16 Tensor Core peak = 312 TFLOP/s; FP32 CUDA-core peak = 19.5 TFLOP/s (NVIDIA published).
Comparison is compute peak vs compute peak, not achievable throughput on any particular kernel.
nonImplications: Does not imply that any real kernel achieves 16× speedup; achievable speedup depends on precision tolerance, kernel implementation, and Roofline regime.
Does not imply that FP16 always improves accuracy-normalized performance; some workloads require careful mixed-precision recipes to preserve accuracy.

distractorRationales.C: Reverses the direction of Tensor Core benefit.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses sparse and dense peak values.
